templates.text: Hiring tip: the best people are never looking. The second best are always looking. You will be interviewing the third best.
Slept eight hours. Woke up with the answer. Not going to pretend that is a repeatable process.
A meeting is a decision that could not be made alone. Most of ours could.
Every roadmap is a work of fiction. The good ones are honest about the genre.
Raising money is not an achievement. It is a debt with better manners.
There is no such thing as a sprint that lasts a year. There is only a company that cannot count.
Users do not want features. Users want their afternoon back.
Process is the scar tissue of a mistake nobody wants to explain twice.
If you need a tooltip to explain the button, the button is the tooltip now.
A metric you cannot move is a mood. Stop putting moods on the wall.
Nobody has ever churned because the price was too high. They churn because the price was too high for that.
The server does not care that it is a weekend. This is the whole job.
Founders love talking about focus in an interview about their six new initiatives.
Everyone who gives advice is describing the company they had, not the one you have.
Growth is not a team. Growth is what happens when the product is good and somebody remembers to tell people.
Best thing about an office: overhearing the bug get fixed. Worst thing: overhearing it get argued about first.
{topic} is not a market. {topic} is a word four companies agreed to use.
Shipping is the only opinion that counts and I say that as somebody who has not shipped this week.
People keep asking what my morning routine is. It is checking whether the company still exists.
Gave an interview. Read it back. Recognised about sixty per cent of it.
{followers} people follow me for opinions about software. I want that on record as their choice.
{product} is close. Close is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
Been heads down on {product} for weeks. It is the best thing {company} has made.
We are building {product} because {topic} has been broken for years and nobody wanted the job.
{product} is out. Go and break it, politely.
Quiet week for {company} on the outside. Not on the inside.
Everything good about {company} was somebody else's idea that I agreed to slowly.
{company} is hiring. Small team, real problems, no ping-pong table and no plans for one.
New build of {product} out. Two features, nine fixes, one apology.
The desk, 11pm. Three monitors, one working.
Whiteboard after the argument. Nobody won.
The team, mid-afternoon, all pretending not to be photographed.
Fourth coffee. The machine and I have an understanding.
The view from the office. It is a wall. It is a very good wall.
Build night. Somebody brought food. Somebody else brought opinions.
Behind the desk. We are going to fix this before anybody important visits.
The wall of stickies. Green is done. There is not much green.
Some studios ship. Some studios announce. Congratulations to {rival} on a great announcement.
Funny how {rival} arrived at exactly our roadmap six weeks after we said it out loud.
If your growth strategy is calling my staff on a Sunday, {rival}, it is not a strategy.
{rival} cut their price again. At some point that stops being aggressive and starts being a confession.
Watched the {rival} demo. Loved the part where it was a video.
Nothing but respect for {rival}. Genuinely. Anyway, we ship on time.
Third person from {rival} in my inbox this month. Not recruiting. They just want to talk.
I am told {rival} has a slide about us. I would like a copy. I would like it framed.

headlines.text: {company}'s founder has found the internet, and the internet has found them back.
{followers} people now read whatever the founder of {company} thinks before breakfast.
The founder of {company} is now quoted more often than the product is used.
A conference has offered {company}'s founder a stage and, as tradition demands, no fee.
Television has entered the chat. {company}'s founder has entered a green room.
{rival} and {company} spent the week talking about each other rather than to customers.
The industry watched two studios explain, at length, that they were not thinking about each other.
Analysts say the {company}–{rival} exchange moved no revenue and a great deal of goodwill.
An old line resurfaced this week. {company}'s founder has been asked about little else.
The archive is undefeated. {company} spent the week in it.

beefLines: Odd to name a company you have never beaten, but go on.
We shipped while you typed. Happy to send the changelog.
This is the third one this month. Are you all right?
I would reply properly but our release is in an hour.
beefReplies: I did not say a name. You did.
Happy to compare release notes any time you like.
Not a fight. An observation, at volume.
Enjoy the announcement. We will enjoy the launch.
Last word is yours. It usually is.
cancelQuotes: Anyone who takes a holiday in year one is not serious about the work.
If you need work-life balance you are not building anything worth balancing.
Most people cannot be trained. Hire the ones who arrive finished.
Our competitors' customers are hostages, not users, and they know it.
I have never taken a day off and I do not intend to start for a wedding.
Sleep is a compounding tax on ambition and I refuse to pay it.
Half of any team is decorative. The trick is finding out which half by December.
